title: Give money a direction beyond yourself
part: III · Money that moves toward others
deck: After zero debt, giving becomes a funded category in the money layer. It trains attention toward the people your work and resources can serve.
question: Can money remain a source of freedom if you can never let any of it leave?

sections.title: The sequence protects the gift
paragraphs: This chapter’s systematic practice begins after the balance sheet has no debt. It does not begin after clearing only the credit card while keeping the mortgage, or after reducing business borrowing to an amount that feels manageable. The sequence is budget, zero debt, then giving.

While debt remains, continue responding to the real needs that arise around you and keep your primary financial effort on getting out of debt. Establish the systematic giving category when the balance sheet is clear.

Once debt is gone, the space it leaves should not flow automatically into consumption and accumulation. Part of the money receives another purpose. Giving becomes something the budget prepares for, rather than something that must defeat every competing desire at the moment a need appears.

Here giving means money. Time, volunteering, introductions and practical assistance can be deeply valuable, but they are not substitutes in the percentage calculation. If you help a neighbor repair something, you have helped your neighbor. You have not thereby funded the monetary category this chapter describes.
sections.principle: Systematic giving begins after zero debt and is funded from the money you actually have.

sections.title: Ten to twenty percent of money, not income
paragraphs: The rule is to assign 10–20% of your current total money to giving. The denominator is the money layer: the cash, bank money and Bitcoin you hold as money within the relevant personal or household system. It is not your salary, annual income, monthly surplus or what remains after every other category feels comfortable.

This is a stock allocation, meaning a share of an existing balance. It is not an annual tax on that balance. Nor is it an instruction to donate the entire percentage today and again tomorrow. The category holds money for a purpose; actual gifts flow from it, and scheduled reviews restore it toward the chosen share as money enters, leaves or changes value.

If your total money is $1,000, the giving category is $100–$200. At $10,000 it is $1,000–$2,000. At $200,000 it is $20,000–$40,000. The principle becomes more demanding as resources grow. A token amount cannot remain the whole practice simply because it felt substantial years earlier.

Giving is inside the money layer, not an extra asset added on top. If a household holds $10,000 in total money and assigns $1,500 to giving, it still has $10,000. The other $8,500 must fund its other monetary purposes. Money already owed to another party is not made available by relabeling it; the no-debt prerequisite and accurate budget come first.

This is why the practice belongs in a household conversation. The amount has to be recognized across all categories. Assigning money to giving while silently expecting the same money to cover rent is not generosity with a strong foundation. Review actual commitments and the overall standard of living so the allocation is real.

example.title: An allocation and a gift
paragraphs: A debt-free household has $10,000 in money and chooses a 15% giving allocation, or $1,500. It then gives $300. With no other change, total money becomes $9,700 and the giving category has $1,200 left.

At the next review, 15% of $9,700 is $1,455. Moving $255 from other monetary categories would restore that target. That movement does not spend another $255; it changes its assigned purpose. Incoming money or other spending will change the calculation, so the review uses current balances.

sections.title: Why the one-sixtieth check appears
paragraphs: The later chapter on net worth introduces a compass: at least one third of assets should be money once debt has gone, with no more than one third in consumption assets and no more than one third in productive assets. Giving belongs inside the first of those groups.

Suppose total debt-free assets are $600,000. One third is $200,000. If the money layer meets that minimum, a 10–20% giving allocation is $20,000–$40,000. Those are meaningful resources with a deliberate outward purpose.

This framework also uses one sixtieth of total assets as a diagnostic threshold. At $600,000, that is $10,000. A giving category below that level prompts a serious check: is money too small a part of the balance sheet, has the giving percentage been misapplied, or has the practice become symbolic?

The arithmetic deserves care. One tenth of one third equals one thirtieth, not one sixtieth. The full minimum implied by one third in money and 10% of money for giving is therefore $20,000 in this example. The $10,000 diagnostic floor is lower; passing it does not establish that the full rule has been met. The checks serve different purposes.
The allocation should be large enough to affect how you see and use your resources. Integrate it accurately with the rest of the household so it becomes a real capacity to help.

sections.title: Prepare some directions; leave some room
paragraphs: A giving category can contain a planned portion and an open portion. Planned giving might support a person through training, a local organization whose work you know or a family facing a sustained difficulty. Open giving leaves room for needs you could not schedule.

If everything is promised in advance, you may have little flexibility when an important need appears nearby. If everything is entirely unplanned, the loudest request can take precedence over the most useful help. A combination provides both continuity and judgment.

A category that never pays out is unfinished. After months of reserving money without making a gift, ask what is preventing action. Perhaps the purpose is vague, the recipient has not been checked or you are waiting for a perfect opportunity that no real person can supply. The answer may be to improve the process, not to abandon the allocation.

Giving should not be restricted to people who already agree with you about Bitcoin. A neighbor needing medicine does not have to pass a monetary theory test. The outward movement matters partly because it brings you into contact with needs and lives beyond your own circle.

example.title: A purpose before the request arrives
paragraphs: A household with $10,000 in total money assigns $1,500 to giving. Within that category, $900 is available for agreed ongoing purposes and $600 remains open for needs that emerge. These are internal assignments, not extra money and not automatic monthly donation amounts.

A verified request for $200 can be met from the open portion without canceling the planned support. The gift is recorded, and the category is brought back toward its target at the next regular allocation review.

sections.title: A request is not an automatic claim
paragraphs: Giving requires judgment. A genuine gift does not demand repayment or hidden loyalty. A loan is a different agreement. Employment pays for work; a recommendation puts your reputation behind someone’s ability. Mixing these can leave both sides resentful.

Sometimes paying a bill directly is more useful than handing over cash. Sometimes a course or tool helps a person who is ready to work. Sometimes the need is simply urgent and the kind response is uncomplicated. Sometimes another transfer would preserve a destructive pattern. Saying no can be responsible, but it should not become a quick way to explain away suffering you have not understood.

People need help after illness, bereavement, injustice and events they did not choose. Help should respect the recipient’s dignity. Good boundaries protect the purpose of the gift and leave the person receiving it room to act.

For a significant gift, verify who is asking and what the money will do. Pressure, secrecy, an urgent change of payment details or a demand for wallet access should stop the transaction until independently checked. A beneficiary never needs your private keys, wallet passphrase or login credentials to receive help.

In a shared household, agree on the decisions that can be made individually and those that require discussion. Keep personal giving separate from company funds. Large gifts, cross-border transfers and gifts from Bitcoin may have legal or tax consequences that depend on the actual people and jurisdictions. Their treatment belongs in the real decision, not in an assumption that a generous purpose settles every other question.

sections.title: Giving does not redeem honest earnings
paragraphs: Money earned through voluntary exchange can record useful work: a problem solved, a reliable product, a deadline kept, a customer served. Profit from that exchange is not something that must be morally washed by a donation. Conversely, donating does not repair dishonest conduct toward a customer or employee.

Giving is connected to work in another way. It trains attention. To give well you must notice what people need, distinguish appearances from causes and learn where a resource can make a difference. Those capacities can also improve how you work, build a service and recognize a worthwhile opportunity.

Systematic giving develops a person’s capacity to create value. Over time it can broaden trust, improve judgment, increase willingness to take appropriate risks and open paths to better earnings. These effects grow through attention, useful work and relationships. A gift leaves the recipient free of any obligation to repay you with an opportunity.

Emily’s story shows that change in practice. After clearing her obligations, she makes giving a genuine share of her money. Helping a neighbor and contributing to a child’s school expense makes her more attentive to people’s practical needs. That attention appears at work too. Someone notices her reliability and introduces her to an employer who needs it. Her usefulness and relationships open the way to a better job.

sections.title: When the money itself can become harder to release
paragraphs: If you expect money to gain purchasing power, every gift can acquire an imaginary future price. A hundred dollars given today becomes all the things its Bitcoin equivalent might buy years from now. Opportunity cost is real, but it cannot be the only fact in a human decision. The person needing help also lives in time.

A funded category settles part of that argument in advance. This share of money has an outward purpose. It may be held in Bitcoin as Bitcoin becomes the household’s primary money, but it does not become an undefined reserve for personal accumulation merely because the exchange rate rises.

At scheduled reviews, value the money consistently. If Bitcoin represents nearly all the money, market changes affect both the total and the giving portion. New receipts, gifts and spending still require reassignment. There is no need to rebuild the budget on every price tick; there is a need not to freeze the category forever at a comfortable old amount.

Giving remains important even if savings eventually cover many years of living costs. The aim is not to become so well protected that no person, project or useful risk can reach you. Work may change with age: less physical effort, more teaching, mentoring, patient investment or careful help. Freedom should enlarge the ways you can contribute, not require that you withdraw from contribution altogether.

Michael and Sarah begin this practice after the house sale and complete debt settlement, then keep it as their money grows. David and Rachel replace irregular grand gestures with agreed directions and careful reviews. Each household develops a form it can sustain. The common discipline is that money moves toward others through a real category and actual decisions.

checks: I understand that systematic giving in this framework starts only after zero debt.
I can calculate 10–20% of current total money without substituting income or monthly surplus.
I understand the difference between maintaining an allocation and donating that percentage every year.
I can explain why one sixtieth is a diagnostic floor and not the full minimum implied by the framework.
I can distinguish a gift from a loan, employment, volunteering and a household obligation.
Where appropriate, I have agreed planned and open giving with the person who shares the money.
summary: Giving is a monetary category after zero debt, funded at 10–20% of the current money layer.
A category needs actual outward transactions, sound judgment and clear boundaries.
Giving trains attention toward others and can strengthen judgment, relationships and the capacity to create value.
